You can use some time expressions with both the simple past and the present perfect:
today, this week / month /year, for (quite) a while, for a long time, recently.
We had some bad luck this year. (The speaker is referring to a point in the past.)
We've had some bad luck this year. (The speaker sees this year as a period of time up to now.)
We've been busy recently. (The speaker may not be busy now but considers this relevant now.)
Time expressions usually go at the beginning or end of a statement.
YesterdayI ran into an old friend.OR / ran into an old friend yesterday.
Use for with a period of time.Use since with a phrase or a clause which gives a point in time.
Don't put a time expression between the verb and the object.
We bought a new television last week. (NOT We bought last week a new television.)
- Avoid putting the time expressions above (except recently) between the subject and the verb.
She got married right after college. (NOT She right after college got married.)
